text: Your last sentence reminds me of this recent post [VIDEO] and it gives such a cool sense of Shenzhen as a place to make and modify things.

story: Chinese engineers cracked Apple's M1 chip and successfully upgrade RAM and SSD
text: There's a video of a western guy living in China learning to desolder Flash memory chips from an iPhone and then solder higher capacity chips in their place from back in 2018. [VIDEO] Being in Shenzhen China, he was able to buy the needed tools and many broken boards to practice on, and eventually managed to do it on a live board himself.

story: How I Made My Own iPhone [video]
text: Another cool episode is where he upgrades a 16GB iPhone to 128GB by soldering a larger flash chip onto the board: [VIDEO]

story: iOS 11.4 to Disable USB Port After 7 Days: What It Means for Mobile Forensics
text: You could just pull the flash chip and image it. You would need to figure out how to get the key, but pulling the flash chip and reading it doesn't look too hard if you can use a heat gun. If you lived in Shenzhen you could go the market and buy a flash reader. Strange Parts is youtube channel where the guy does this. [VIDEO]
